newsitem.title: SPAIN: Tens of thousands protest in Madrid against budget.
newsitem.headline: Tens of thousands protest in Madrid against budget.

text.p: Tens of thousands of people marched through central Madrid on Saturday in protest at a public sector pay freeze included in the conservative government's strict 1997 budget for Spain.

Union leaders said more than 200,000 people took part in the rally, which ended at the Plaza de Espana central square. They called for a general strike in the near future and promised to block highways and stage other protests to force the government into talks.

"We will continue to fight for real round-table negotiations on a salaries agreement for the whole term of government," the leader of the umbrella union for public employees, Domingo Fernandez, told the rally.
He condemned the pay freeze as unjust because the government had not asked for sacrifices from people with high incomes.
"It's an attack on society's cohesion," Fernadez said. "If you lose the confidence and cooperation of the public employees and their unions, you lose the battle."
The plaza was filled with workers and families who gave the protest a carnival atmosphere with balloons, whistles and colourful banners.

"I'm here and my whole family is here. They keep asking us for sacrifices for the future of Spain, but what about my children, what about their future. There is no price for that," said a government worker, who asked not to be identified.

Conservative Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar, whose government prepared a strict budget to get Spain in financial shape for Europe's single currency, told a conference on Saturday that the sacrifices he demanded were reasonable.

"We will thoroughly study their concerns and demands, but I'm very conscious that I have asked them for an effort and it is a worthwhile one," Aznar said at a conference on welfare in Salamanca. "This (pay freeze) is a reasonable decision."
Union leaders said new protest measures would be decided at a meeting on 28th November.
